title: Soft-throttle shaping and timeout inheritance for reranking service
creator: Maya Chen
description: Add a multi-layered, load-aware soft-throttling and timeout inheritance system for the reranking endpoint to improve P95/P99 latency stability under bursty traffic and regional capacity loss. The feature combines: (1) soft admission control (shaping) at edge and regional gateways, (2) timeout inheritance so downstream model ops inherit upstream remaining budget, and (3) a small set of lightweight circuit templates that our smart router can apply per-tenant and per-route. The goal is predictable latency SLOs and fewer high-latency tails without hard rejecting production queries unless necessary.
acceptance_criteria: Soft-throttle accepts shaping directives from Console and defaults to safe profiles for public tenants
Timeout inheritance implemented end-to-end: router -> regional gateway -> model worker and validated in unit + e2e tests
P95 latency for critical rerank flows improves by at least 30% under simulated burst traffic compared to baseline
Circuit templates (conservative, balanced, aggressive) are configurable per-project via API and appear in Rollouts UI
No increase in error rate for low-volume tenants in canary region after 2-day canary
Documentation and runbook added with rollback steps and metrics to observe
tasks: Design soft-throttle admission API and default profiles (edge/regional)
Prototype timeout propagation header and worker-side enforcement patch
Implement router-side logic to select circuit template based on tenant SLA and current capacity
Add metrics and dashboards: shaping_rejections, shaping_delay_ms, timeout_budget_remaining, circuit_state_transitions
End-to-end test harness: k6 traffic spike scenarios and multi-region failover
Canary deploy to staging-alpha, run 48-hour traffic replay, validate SLOs
Rollout to production with stepdown policy and automated rollback
metrics_baseline: Baseline P95 for rerank-critical flow: 240ms under steady load; P95 under 3x burst: 1.2s. Target after changes: P95 < 850ms under 3x burst and steady-state P95 reduction >= 30%.
implementation_plan: Week 1: finalize API and profiles; Week 2: implement timeout header propagation and worker enforcement; Week 3: integrate router circuit template selection and metrics; Week 4: run canary and iterate on profiles. Use feature flag gating per-region. Start with conservative profile in EU and NA, aggressive only after validation in staging.
technical_notes: Timeout inheritance uses X-Rerank-Time-Budget-ms header. Router calculates remaining budget after routing, subtracts estimated network overhead, and forwards header. Worker enforces a soft-deadline that allows graceful partial results if near-exhaustion. Admission control implements token-bucket shaping with request metadata (route, tenant, priority). Circuit templates are small state machines (CLOSED, SOFT_OPEN, OPEN) with exponential backoff and probe windows; soft_open allows limited hedged probes to preferred region.
risks: Incorrect budget calculation could silently truncate responses leading to quality regressions
Shaping too aggressive may increase tail latency for important tenants if profiles misconfigured
Telemetry gaps may make it hard to diagnose when shaping causes increased downstream latency
Interplay with existing autoscaler policies could trigger oscillations if not coordinated

notes: This ticket focuses on behavior and controls for maintaining late-tail latency for reranking. Separate tickets will address model-level optimizations (quantization, KV cache prewarm) and embedding cache alignment. Coordinate with Console team to expose profiles in Rollouts UI.
postmortem_hooks: If a production incident occurs during rollout, capture shaping_rejections, timeout_budget_histogram, and circuit_state_transitions for last 60 minutes and attach to incident. Include canary-region logs and probe traces.
rollback_plan: Flip feature flag off at router and gateway layers which immediately disables shaping and timeout header injection; worker will accept full default budget. If issue persists after flag off, revert worker enforcement patch. Ops to run emergency-scaleup policy if error rate rises.
